comments: Final ALLFRAME+TRIAL solution from 7 of 11 Cepheids with P>20 d; shorter-period stars were excluded for incompleteness. Hill et al. calibration and R_V=3.3 were adopted. No metallicity correction enters this modulus.

Alternative solution obtained by applying the standard Key Project PL fit to the original Tanvir et al. photometry. It uses seven long-period Cepheids and is not the paper's preferred ALLFRAME distance.

Uncorrected re-fit of seven previously selected Cepheids using the Stetson WFPC2 zero point, Udalski OGLE-LMC PL relations and mu_LMC=18.45. The error is the internal R_PL term; no galaxy-specific systematic error is tabulated.

Metallicity-corrected counterpart of the same seven-star fit, using gamma_VI=-0.2 mag dex^-1 and the adopted field abundance. The correction raises the modulus by 0.140 mag; e_R remains the internal R_PL term.
HST V,I data originally from Tanvir et al. and reanalyzed by the Key Project. The quoted error is random only. A common LMC zero-point uncertainty of about 0.2 mag is discussed but not included.
Final period-cut Wesenheit fit before abundance correction. e_R is the random PL-fit error only; N_cef is the post-cut sample.
Table 4 mu_Z, using gamma=-0.2 mag dex^-1 relative to the LMC. Metallicity uncertainty is systematic and excluded from e_R.
Preferred near-solar-metallicity solution with modest Vlim sensitivity (+0.09/-0.05 mag). Table 6 reports 74 sosie matches rather than a verified number of unique Cepheids.
Present-paper HIPPARCOS-calibrated PL solution. The quoted uncertainty is internal. Incompleteness, extinction, zero-point and PL-slope effects are discussed separately.

Final period-dependent metallicity-corrected modulus. The uncorrected GC/LMC routes give 30.25/30.02 mag. Strong residual period dependence suggests that the formal error may understate the true uncertainty.

Direct archival HST/WFPC2 measurement. Population I regions were excised and the edge response was weighted by sqrt(LF). I_TRGB=25.66+/-0.28 and A_I=0.05. No separate mu_0 error is tabulated; e_R follows the tip uncertainty.
Measurement error is 0.03 mag, with an additional 0.12 mag systematic. Internal RGB extinction is assumed negligible. The result is 0.50 mag larger than the earlier TRGB estimate.
Combined NGC 4258+LMC blue-I solution from reprocessed HST/ACS outer-field photometry (R_GC>=3.5 arcmin). Error is random only; the common calibration systematic is 0.057 mag.
Preferred color-corrected QT solution on the combined NGC 4258+LMC scale. Artificial-star corrections were applied. Error is random only; systematic=0.057 mag.
The TRGB lies less than 1 mag above the detection limit, so the distance may be underestimated. M_I=-4.0+/-0.2 averages over unknown metallicity; only foreground extinction is used.
